# Held out results

*Generated by `python -m antenatal holdout-report` on {stamp} from the tables the single held out evaluation wrote, the access log, the integrity audits and git. Nothing was fitted and the held out records were not read to produce this page. The protocol fixed before the run is `docs/holdout_protocol.md`.*

The held out records are {n} pregnancies with {events} recorded low birth weight births. They were set aside before any model was fitted and evaluated once, at {evaluated}, on models locked beforehand. Nothing about the models changes because of these results.

## 1. Proof that the model did not learn from the held out records

The supervisor asked that the held out records never be found in the training pipeline, so that the model could not be biased by them. Five separate kinds of evidence show this.

**1. The order of events, from git.** The held out records were sealed before the served model was fitted, every locked model was fixed before the held out outcomes were first read, and no locked model changed afterwards.

{timeline}

**2. The integrity audit, before and after.** `python -m antenatal audit-holdout` checks, without reading any held out outcome, that no held out record is in the development data, that no registration group is split between the two, that the training guard refuses every held out record, that no saved prediction file contains a held out record, that the served model reproduces the development out of fold predictions, and that no held out record has a predictor vector identical to a development record. Before the run {before} of {total} checks passed (`{evidence}/audit_before.txt`, committed before the run); after the run {after} of {total} passed (`docs/evidence/holdout_integrity.md`).

**3. The guard in code.** Every model fit carries a `TrainingGuard` that raises an error if any held out record is present, and every step that learns from data (imputation, scaling, the availability screen, tuning) runs inside the training fold.

**4. Rebuilding the model from development records alone.** `tests/integration/test_artefact_reproducibility.py` refits the served pipeline on the 3,126 development records only and checks that its feature names, coefficients, intercept and reference probabilities equal those of the committed model to within 1e-9. A model that had seen any held out record could not be rebuilt exactly without it.

**5. One read, logged.** `partitions/holdout_access.log` holds {log_lines} lines: the opening of the partition, {evaluations} evaluation with the operator, purpose, commit and every checksum, and {refused} refused attempt to evaluate again.

**What the results themselves show.** A model that had learned from the held out records would score clearly better on them than on unseen development records. The table compares the served model on both.

{consistency}
